sections.overview: Protanguilla palau is a small eel discovered in a submerged reef cave in Palau; it is the sole known species of its family, Protanguillidae.
sections.identification: Its anatomy combines traits seen in living eels with features otherwise known from fossil eels, which led researchers to describe a new family and a deeply branching eel lineage.
sections.habitat: The type specimens came from a fringing-reef cave about 35 m deep in Palau, in the western Pacific.
sections.diet: The original description does not establish what this eel eats in the wild.
sections.behavior: Its known records are from a marine cave; the available description does not provide a detailed account of its daily behavior.
sections.reproduction: Reproductive biology remains undocumented in the sources consulted.
sections.ecology: Phylogenetic analyses place it as a very early-diverging branch among living true eels; “living fossil” is a popular shorthand, not a literal claim that the species has remained unchanged.
sections.conservation: The IUCN Red List assessment published in 2019 classified the species as Data Deficient, reflecting limited information for assessing its extinction risk.
